title: OU's First College Football Playoff Game: 2015 Orange Bowl vs Clemson
question: When did Oklahoma make its first College Football Playoff appearance?
answer: Oklahoma's first College Football Playoff game was the Orange Bowl semifinal on December 31, 2015. The No. 4 Sooners led No. 1 Clemson 17-16 at halftime but lost 37-17.
summary: OU's first College Football Playoff game was the Dec. 31, 2015 Orange Bowl semifinal. The Sooners led Clemson 17-16 at the half before falling 37-17.
body: A year after an 8-5 finish that ended with a bowl loss to Clemson, Bob Stoops reshaped his staff, and the 2015 Sooners surged into the second edition of the College Football Playoff as the No. 4 seed. Their semifinal opponent was a familiar one: unbeaten, top-ranked Clemson, in the Orange Bowl in Miami Gardens.

The first half went Oklahoma's way. Samaje Perine capped the opening drive with a 1-yard touchdown, and Baker Mayfield found Mark Andrews for an 11-yard score with 1:34 left before halftime. The Sooner defense then intercepted a Deshaun Watson throw in the end zone, and OU carried a 17-16 lead into the locker room. The Sooners had averaged 52 points over their previous seven games.

Clemson owned the second half. The Tigers took the second-half kickoff 75 yards for Wayne Gallman's 1-yard touchdown, added a 35-yard Watson touchdown pass to Hunter Renfrow, and blanked Oklahoma the rest of the way. Watson accounted for 332 yards, including 145 on the ground, and Clemson piled up 550 total yards. Mayfield threw for 311 yards but was intercepted twice, and OU ran for just 67 yards.

That night began a hard playoff stretch. Oklahoma returned to the semifinals after the 2017, 2018 and 2019 seasons and lost each time, then fell 34-24 to Alabama in a first-round game in Norman in December 2025.
